title: Daughter Searches for Parents After Nepal Floods
summary:
Imagine not being able to reach your parents for days. That's what Shreya Ahuja is going through right now.

Shreya is a doctor who lives in North Carolina. Her parents, Deepak and Madhu Ahuja, went on a special trip to Mount Kailash for her dad's 60th birthday. They were walking back toward the border when huge floods hit Nepal.

Shreya talked to them just hours before the floods. The next morning, she saw messages about flash flooding. She tried to call and text them, but no answer. "I feel like everyone thinks, what are the chances that they were in that exact spot?" she said.

The floods were terrible. Nearly 30-foot-high waves rushed down a river between Tibet and Nepal. More than 500 people died, and over 1,500 are still missing. Shreya's parents were last seen at the Gyirong border crossing. CCTV footage shows the building where their group was supposed to be got destroyed.

Shreya is now in Washington, D.C., with her grandparents. She hasn't slept much. "It's essentially been one long day," she said.

She's asking for help. She wants governments to work together and for Starlink to be allowed in Nepal so people can communicate. "These are all tangible things that could really help us get into contact with people on the ground," she said.

We hope Shreya finds her parents safe and sound.
why_it_matters: This story shows why fast communication and countries working together can help save people during natural disasters.

background_read: Nepal is a country in South Asia next to Tibet (a region of China), and Mount Kailash is a very tall mountain in Asia that people visit for special trips.
Shreya's parents were walking back toward the border after visiting it when huge floods hit, and they were last seen at the Gyirong border crossing.
Shreya wants governments to work together and Starlink (a company that gives internet through satellites) to be allowed in Nepal so people can communicate.
Article_Structure: WHO: Shreya Ahuja, a doctor in North Carolina, and her missing parents Deepak and Madhu Ahuja.
WHAT: Shreya is trying to find her parents after flash floods destroyed the building where their group was supposed to be.
WHERE: The Gyirong border crossing between Tibet and Nepal; Shreya is in Washington, D.C.
WHY: Because the floods killed more than 500 people and left over 1,500 missing, including her parents.

perspectives.description: They are desperate for any help, and they hope governments will work together to find missing people.
They need better communication tools, like satellite internet, to reach people cut off by the floods.
They see this as a reminder that natural disasters can hit suddenly and that communication can save lives.
